reviewer: adversarial finder (score not authoritative; see PROMPT-STANDARD "How to review a prompt")

gaps.problem: Item 16 cannot be satisfied as literally written. The domain is restricted to 'cells with getHeight > seaLevel + 45', so every channel cell is above 45 m by construction — yet the item then counts only components 'whose lowest cell is below seaLevel + 45'. Under the binding reading the count is always 0 and the item always fails; under the charitable reading (the channel must drain to below 45 m) the domain restriction has to be dropped, and D8 accumulation over a truncated domain is ill-defined anyway because flow entering from outside is discarded. Two agents will read this two ways and the round is spent arguing about it.
gaps.fix: Rewrite as: compute D8 flow accumulation over the whole 513² grid; a channel cell has accumulation ≥ 200 cells AND getHeight > seaLevel + 45; count connected components of ≥ 40 such cells whose downstream continuation reaches a cell below seaLevel + 45 (follow the D8 pointer from the component's lowest cell until it drops below 45 m or leaves the grid); require ≥ 8.

gaps.property: 3. Numeric / 4. Anchored (the worked example fails its own test)
gaps.problem: The item 17 reconciliation note — the one place the spec says 'the round is lost if the builder guesses' — hands a range whose corners fail the tests it claims to satisfy. Item 2(b) grades p90/p10 of the Lambert term, not the extremes. For h = A·sin(2πx/λ) with sun at 8.46°, the slope angle has an arcsine distribution, so p90/p10 uses θ = ±0.951·θmax. At the stated corner A = 1.5 m, λ = 200 m: θmax = 2.70°, ratio = sin(11.03°)/sin(5.89°) = 1.86 — fails the ≥ 2.5 floor. At the other corner A = 2.5 m, λ = 120 m: max grade 13.1 %, which blows item 17's ≤ 5.5 % mean grade. Only the worked pair (A = 2, λ = 170) passes, and even that gives 2.79 rather than the quoted 2.9 (the quoted figure is the extreme ratio, not the percentile ratio), and it degrades further for an isotropic 2D undulation where the slope component along the sun azimuth is reduced. A builder who takes the range at its word ships a plain that fails item 2(b) or item 17.
gaps.fix: Replace the range with the constraint that actually binds: require max grade 2πA/λ ∈ [6.5 %, 7.8 %] (e.g. A = 2.0 m at λ = 165-175 m), state that the undulation must be anisotropic with its dominant ridge axis within 30° of north-south so the 06.5/17.5 sun rakes across it, and show the percentile arithmetic (p90/p10 = sin(e + 0.951·θmax)/sin(e − 0.951·θmax) = 2.79 at A = 2, λ = 170) rather than the extreme-value arithmetic, so the builder sizes against the number the critic will actually compute.

gaps.problem: Three items are presented as mechanical but leave the sample selection to the grader, so two critics get two numbers from the same frame. Item 2(a): 'among those take one with sunLit() === true and one with sunLit() === false within 300 m of it' — no ordering, no tie-break, and a 64×64 patch centred on a candidate near a shadow boundary is contaminated by the other state. Item 3: 'overlay a 3×3 grid of 80×80 px patches' — the grid's origin is never given, and there is no rule for what happens when a centre lands on water, on rock, or outside item 17's plain mask, which at the aerial camera (520 m, target origin, plain mask only ±600 m) is close to certain. Item 13: 'three sites ≥ 300 m apart' with no rule for which three.
gaps.fix: Make each selection deterministic in the probe. Item 2(a): enumerate every qualifying pair in raster order, discard pairs whose 64×64 patches are not ≥ 90 % same-lit-state and same cover.id by the per-pixel groundmap, and grade the MEDIAN ratio over the qualifying pairs, reporting the count. Item 3: fix the grid at centres (px, py) = (120 + 120i, 55 + 80j) in 480-wide space, and specify that a disqualified centre is replaced by the nearest qualifying pixel within 40 px, with the item failing only if fewer than 7 of 9 patches qualify. Item 13: sample coast normals every 25 m of arc length, take the three sites at the 10th, 50th and 90th percentile of measured beach width.

gaps.property: 2. Falsifiable (named observation method cannot produce the number)
gaps.problem: Two of the seven budget rows are ungradeable. 'Heap added ≤ 80 MB — `__sim.stats().heapMB` delta with `debug.setTerrain(false)`' cannot work: `setTerrain` only sets `S.mesh.group.visible` (src/modules/terrain/index.js), it disposes nothing, so the delta is ~0 regardless of what the module allocates; and GPU texture memory is not in the JS heap at all. 'GPU texture memory owned by terrain ≤ 120 MB' has no measurement method in the 'How it is checked' column — it lists the intended composition instead. A row nobody can measure is a row that gets waved through, which is how the budget creep in §6 happened.
gaps.fix: Grade heap as a boot-time delta instead: `__sim.stats().heapMB` at `?showcase=environment` versus `?showcase=terrain`, both after `window.__sim.ready` plus 60 frames, ≤ 80 MB. Grade texture memory as a computed number the probe can produce: sum over `renderer.info.memory.textures` entries is only a count, so instead require the builder to log a `texBytes` line from its own allocation sites (width·height·bpp·1.33 for mipmapped) and have the critic check that log against the 120 MB cap and against `renderer.info.memory.textures` for the count.

gaps.property: Rules for role prompts (duplication that has already drifted)
gaps.problem: The 'Measurement conventions' block is copied into terrain.md, roads.md, props.md, effects.md and audio.md — the spec says so itself and asks the integrator to move it. It has already drifted: roads.md:144 defines L with no downsample at all, props.md:186-189 fixes a different measurement scale and defines saturation as 'HSV S', while terrain.md defines the 480-wide box-filter downsample and sat as mean (max−min)/max. Same word, three definitions, five files. Every future change to the convention is five edits and a silent inconsistency between what a builder targets and what a critic measures.
gaps.fix: Move the conventions paragraph verbatim into CRITIC.md under a heading the specs can cite ('CRITIC.md §Measurement'), delete it from all five module specs, and leave in terrain.md only the two terrain-specific definitions (GROUND BAND and the ground probe). Since terrain's version is the most complete, promote that text and reconcile roads.md/props.md to it in the same edit.

gaps.problem: Item 1's noon thresholds are half-derived. `std ≥ 26` gets a careful derivation from the 21-24 single-cover and 39.3 whole-frame anchors — that is the best passage in the spec. But `p95 ≥ 150` is supported by nothing: the primary reference cs2_2's whole frame measures p5-p95 = 21-142, so CS2 itself fails the item by 8 levels, and the near forested slope crop (20-87) fails it by 63. The sat floors (0.22 noon, 0.28 golden hour) are likewise asserted, sitting between the 0.141 far-crop and 0.346 near-slope anchors with no stated reasoning. Chasing p95 ≥ 150 through albedo is exactly the pressure that produced 'bleached noon' in §6, and terrain cannot use exposure to get there because environment owns it.
gaps.fix: Either derive p95 and sat the way std is derived (state which anchor blend they come from and why SimBuild's cover mix should sit above cs2_2's 142), or drop p95 to a value the reference supports (≥ 140) and restate the intent as a spread requirement: p95 − p5 ≥ 55 at noon, which cs2_2's whole frame (121) clears comfortably and r1's 118-146 (28) fails by the same margin the current wording intends.

gaps.property: 2. Falsifiable (test measures the wrong thing on one of its two frames)
gaps.problem: Item 4 runs the tiling autocorrelation over the GROUND BAND of `coast_12.png`. For the `coast` preset the GROUND BAND is the bottom 45 % of a frame aimed over the estuary toward the sea, i.e. mostly water — and the water surface is normal-mapped from `makeRippleNormal(..., 256, ...)`, a genuinely periodic 256² texture. The item will detect a periodic echo that is the ripple map, not the ground splat it is written to police, and items 3 and 5 already show the spec knows how to exclude water via the ground probe.
gaps.fix: Add to item 4: 'restricted to pixels the ground probe reports as `water === false`; if fewer than 40 % of a frame's GROUND BAND pixels are non-water, substitute `valley_12.png` for that frame.' Also pin the two loose ends in the reference implementation — `boxblur16` clamps at the border, and the 9-shift moving average is computed only over shifts with a full window (s = 8..124).

gaps.property: 1. Sequenced / 2. Falsifiable (cross-module dependency with no escape hatch)
gaps.problem: Item 14 requires terrain to use environment's fog uniforms and forbids it from adding its own, and item 1 plus the §8 aerial row require 'near-clear inside 800 m'. But r1's blocker 2 was caused in part by environment's haze reaching ~30 % at 500-700 m, the haze cap is an open ask in docs/core-requests/terrain.md ('keep fogDensity ≤ 3 % at 500 m for a camera 400 m up'), and the standing assumptions resolve only the exposure half of the problem ('terrain compensates in albedo') while naming fog as environment-owned with no remedy. Terrain can fail an acceptance item through a neighbour's parameter it is explicitly barred from touching.
gaps.fix: State the current measured `world.weather.fogDensity` for the `partly` preset and the status of that core request in the standing assumptions, and add the escape: 'if the probe reads fogDensity above <value> at capture, record it in the build record, file the core request, and items 14(a) and 1's near-clear clause are graded against the transmittance that density implies rather than as a terrain failure.'

gaps.property: 5. Bounded blast radius (conflict with a role file)
gaps.problem: §5 instructs `budget: { drawCalls: 25 }` and then tells the critic to grade `summary.json.maxDrawCalls` — a whole-frame number — against 40. CRITIC.md's pass condition is 'draw calls within the declared budget' and its hard-fail list is read off the same summary.json. Read literally, a terrain frame at 30-40 whole-frame draws fails against a declared 25. The reconciliation is correct on the ARCHITECTURE §9 reading (terrain 20 + water 5, environment 15 separately) but it lives in the module spec, where it changes nothing about how the critic's role file reads, so it will be argued again next round and again in roads.md.
gaps.fix: Put the rule in CRITIC.md: 'draw calls are graded per-module against the module's declared budget using the toggle delta, and whole-frame `maxDrawCalls` against the module's §9 allowance plus environment's 15.' Then terrain.md only needs to name its two numbers (25 attributable, 40 whole-frame) and can drop the argument.

gaps.problem: Acceptance items name `coast_17p5.png`, `coast_22.png`, `ridge_12.png`, `skyline_6p5.png`, `closeup_12.png`, the two 720p frames, the groundmap JSONs and the `?showcase=all` frame — but CRITIC.md's routine is 4 cameras × 12/22 plus declared presets at 12 and 22, and §8 reinforces 'all three are shot by the critic at 12 and 22'. `coast_17p5` is required by item 12(c) and produced by neither. A missing shot is an ungraded item, which is a round.
gaps.fix: Add a short table at the end of §4 listing every artefact the checklist consumes — camera, time, resolution, and the item(s) that read it — and one gauntlet/screenshot command line that produces the set. Item 12(c) in particular needs `--camera coast --time 17.5` called out explicitly.

gaps.problem: Item 15 is the one item in the list that is an opinion in checklist clothing: 'a 4× crop of a valley-wall shadow edge shows no staircase with steps ≥ 8 m and no blobbing.' Which crop, chosen by whom, is not stated; 'no blobbing' has no definition; and there is no way to convert a step measured in a 4× pixel crop into 8 metres without the groundmap's world positions, which the item never invokes even though the probe that provides them is defined two pages earlier.
gaps.fix: Rewrite against the groundmap: locate the shadow edge as the set of pixels where `sunLit()` flips between 8 px neighbours, fit a line to that boundary over a 128 px run, and require that the RMS deviation of the boundary from the fit is ≤ 2 m in world units (from the groundmap's per-pixel positions), with no single excursion ≥ 8 m. Drop 'no blobbing' or replace it with a stated minimum boundary length per connected shadow region.

gaps.property: 3. Numeric (thresholds measured inside frames the builder frames)
gaps.problem: Items 10, 12 and 13 are graded as a percentage of frames from `ridge` and `coast` — presets the builder itself declares in §8. Item 10's 'snow pixels are 0.5-6 % of the GROUND BAND in ridge_12' is partly satisfied by choosing the ridge camera's pitch and distance rather than by building the snow layer. §8's 'Must show' column constrains `valley` numerically (≥ 18 m of relief) but leaves `ridge` and `coast` as prose.
gaps.fix: Give ridge and coast the same treatment as valley: for `ridge`, require ≥ 4 of item 9(b)'s summits inside the frustum and the ridge crest occupying 25-45 % of frame height; for `coast`, require the island and ≥ 300 m of waterline in frame. Then a percentage-of-frame threshold means something.

gaps.problem: Three small ones. (a) §7 sources the extra `world.weather` fields to 'ARCHITECTURE §3 + the integrator's §3 addendum' — there is no addendum in ARCHITECTURE.md; the fields are real (environment/index.js:275-281 publishes moonDir, lightDir, exposure, night) but a builder sent to a non-existent section will either guess or stop. (b) The texture budget is tighter than it reads: six 1k PBR sets at map+normal+arm with mipmaps is ~96 MB, plus height/derived/land/macro/ripple and a 768² half-float reflection RT lands near 107 MB of the 120 MB cap, so the 'a snow/frost set is the only justified addition' allowance (~+16 MB) would breach it. (c) The ground probe is specified to dump a per-pixel map, i.e. up to 129 600 JS raycasts through `data.raycast`'s 4000-iteration march, on a box where captures already run to a 240 s timeout, with no stride or time budget given.
gaps.fix: (a) Cite `src/modules/environment/index.js:275-281` as the source of truth for the published weather fields, and file the §3 addendum as a core request. (b) State the measured current texture total and say the snow set is justified only if it replaces one of the six, or lift the cap to 140 MB against §9's 768 MB scene budget. (c) Specify the groundmap stride (e.g. every 2nd pixel, upsampled for crop tests) and a ≤ 60 s probe budget.

strengths: World-data signatures are literally copied from ARCHITECTURE §3, stray comma in `modify(brush) ,` included, and every addition (`version`, `writeHeights`, `flattenStrip`, `features`, `serialize`) is flagged AS an addition with the integrator ruling that authorises it (docs/core-requests/terrain.md). This is exactly what the standard asks for and most specs paraphrase instead.

Named dependency APIs are real, and I spot-checked them: all ten environment functions exist at src/modules/environment/index.js:296-323; `sunDirectionAt` at :44 does return a direction toward the light (`y = sin(elevation)`), which is what the probe's `sunLit()` assumes; the roads guard is quoted verbatim from src/modules/terrain/detail.js:161; the four core presets match src/core/camera.js:23-27; `assets.pbr` is documented with `armMap`/`entry` per src/core/assets.js rather than ARCHITECTURE §6's shorter list; the existing terrain `api`/`debug` list matches src/modules/terrain/index.js exactly.

The derived numbers check out. `clock.sunElevation(6.5) = 0.1476 rad = 8.46°`, 64.8° at 12 and -56° at 22 all reproduce from src/core/clock.js:35. The skyline camera position (718, 183, -523) reproduces from camera.js `updateCamera()` with yaw 2.2 / pitch 0.16 / d 900 / target [0,40,0], and the 2330 m far corner is right. A builder can trust the geometry it is handed.

Known failure modes are this project's, not generic: every bullet in §6 maps onto a ranked issue in docs/critic/terrain_r1.json (blocker 1 confetti, blocker 2 milky aerial, 3 sprite tufts, 4 self-lit night tufts, 5 spire/cone/hard skirt, 6 pink shore, 7 stair-stepped shadows, 8 brush-stroke swirl, 9 weak reflections, 10 valley with no valley) plus r2's self-flagged 17-30 m fade band, 1 018 696 triangles and 19 draws from docs/builds/terrain_r2.json.

The reference table disqualifies five of the eight CS2 images with a stated reason, and scopes cs2_6 to 'banding shape only' with an explicit ban on using it for items 10 and 14. That kills a whole class of mis-calibration a critic would otherwise re-litigate every round.

Item 4's tiling test is validated before it is imposed: measured on four reference crops (0.048-0.074) and on two synthetic motifs (0.251, 0.322), so the 0.20 threshold has demonstrated separation instead of being a guess.

The budget section resolves a genuine three-way conflict in the open: §4's illustrative 400 k, the code's declared 1 300 000 and §9's 3 M scene cap, and reads §9's 'terrain 20 + water 5' correctly since water is terrain-owned.

§7's degrade clauses and the standing-assumptions block make the module genuinely autonomous: absent environment, absent `world.roads.isRoad`, missing `coverAt` (item 10 names a fallback classifier) are all pre-decided.
verdict: A genuinely strong spec that falls short of pass on arithmetic and procedure, not on ambition. The world-data block is copied from ARCHITECTURE §3 rather than paraphrased, every added API is justified by a named integrator ruling, the dependency APIs I checked all exist at the lines cited, the sun-elevation and skyline-camera derivations reproduce exactly from src/core, and the known failure modes map one-to-one onto terrain_r1's ranked issues and r2's build record — no generic advice anywhere. Roughly 19 of 24 acceptance items are mechanically gradeable, which is well above the norm. But item 16 is unsatisfiable as literally written; the item 17 reconciliation note, the passage that exists specifically to stop the builder guessing, hands a 1.5-2.5 m / 120-200 m range whose corners fail item 2(b) (1.86 against a 2.5 floor) and item 17 (13 % grade) respectively, and quotes an extreme-value ratio where the test computes a percentile ratio; items 2(a), 3 and 13 leave sample selection to the grader so two critics get two numbers; the heap and texture-memory budget rows name measurement methods that cannot produce a number (`debug.setTerrain(false)` only toggles visibility); and the measurement-conventions block the spec knowingly duplicates into four other specs has already drifted three ways. Fix the two arithmetic traps and the three selection procedures and this is a 9.
